subject: body
title: Heart and Blood
about: Deeper than Heart, Lungs and Bones: the heart as a fist-sized pump with four rooms behind the breastbone, blood vessels and the veins he can see, blood carrying oxygen from the lungs and taking carbon dioxide back, the pulse at his wrist, a heartbeat that is slowest in sleep, blood that is red and mostly water, how blood thickens to stop a cut bleeding and what to do for a small cut, and what the heart loves. Inside-the-body anatomy is a bridge topic beyond NC Grade 1; the nearest codes are PE.1.HF.3.1 and PE.1.HF.3.2 (the heart and lungs in fitness) and 1.NPA.1.1 and 1.NPA.2.1 (water and activity). Read it together: the tablet reads every card aloud while he finds his own pulse.
tip: Help him press two fingers on the inside of his wrist and count beats for ten seconds, then jump for a minute and count again.

cards.q: Squeeze your fist, open it, squeeze again. Your heart works like that. What is it squeezing out?
cards.note: Each squeeze pushes blood out into your body. Each time it opens, it fills up again.

cards.q: Make a fist. Which part inside you is about that same size?
cards.note: Your heart grows as your fist grows. A grown-up's heart is about the size of a grown-up's fist.

cards.q: Your heart sits in the middle of your chest, tipped a little left. Which hard bone is right in front of it?
cards.note: Put a hand flat on the middle of your chest to feel the breastbone. It and the ribs make a strong cage around the heart.

cards.q: Blood travels around your body inside tiny tubes. What are the tubes called?
cards.note: The biggest vessels are as wide as a finger. The tiniest are thinner than a hair.

cards.q: Some people can see blue or green lines under the skin on their wrist. What are they?
cards.note: Veins carry blood back to the heart. The blood inside is red; a vein only looks blue or green through your skin, and on some skin it does not show at all.

cards.q: Blood picks something up in your lungs and delivers it to every part of you. What is it?
cards.note: Oxygen is a gas in the air. Every part of your body needs it to work.

cards.q: Blood also carries away a used-up gas your body wants to get rid of. Where does it drop it off?
cards.note: The gas is carbon dioxide. You breathe it out, and the blood heads back for more oxygen.

cards.q: When does your heart beat the slowest?
cards.note: A sleeping body needs the least blood, so the heart takes it easy. It still never stops.

cards.q: Press two fingers on the inside of your wrist. What is the little beat you feel?
cards.note: Each pulse is a push of blood from one heartbeat. You can feel it on the side of your neck too.

cards.q: Why does the doctor listen to your chest with a stethoscope?
cards.note: Say STETH-uh-scope. The doctor listens to the lub-dub of your heart and the whoosh of your lungs.

cards.q: A small cut bleeds, then the bleeding stops all by itself. How does blood do that?
cards.note: Tiny bits in your blood stick together and make a plug. The plug dries into a scab while new skin grows under it.

cards.q: You get a small cut on your finger. What should you do?
cards.note: Rinse with clean water, pat dry, put on a bandage and tell a grown-up.
Blood is always red, bright red when it is full of oxygen and darker red when it is not.

cards.q: Blood is mostly made of something you drink every day. What is it?
cards.note: More than half of your blood is water. Drinking water keeps blood flowing smoothly.

cards.q: Your heart has little rooms inside, with doors that open and shut. How many rooms?
cards.note: Two rooms on top fill up with blood, two on the bottom pump it out. The lub-dub sound is the little doors snapping shut.

cards.q: Which three things keep your heart strong and happy?
cards.note: Running, biking and swimming make the heart muscle stronger. Water and good food keep the blood healthy.
